title: Data Collection Facts Label
text:
Data Source Facts Label














Source Identity






Source name


2024 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS), Combined Landline and Cell Phone Data




Domain/topic


Public health, population health, demographics, health behaviors, chronic conditions, health care access, and health related quality of life among U.S. adults




Source type


Federal government public use survey dataset produced through a state based health surveillance system











Collection Context






Collector/producer


The Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System is coordinated by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). State and territorial health departments administer the survey directly or through contracted telephone survey organizations




Original purpose


BRFSS was created for ongoing public health surveillance. It collects state specific information about health related risk behaviors, chronic health conditions, health care access, preventive service use, and selected demographic characteristics so public health agencies can monitor populations, plan programs, establish priorities, and evaluate health initiatives




Collection method


Data are collected throughout the year through computer assisted telephone interviews. Participating states use random digit dialed landline and cellular telephone samples. Interviewers administer a standardized core questionnaire, with optional modules and state added questions. The health and demographic responses used in this dataset are primarily self reported rather than obtained from medical examinations or records




Record creation event


A respondent level record is created when an eligible adult is selected and interviewed through the BRFSS telephone survey and the interview is retained for the public use dataset. Each included record contains that respondent’s coded answers plus calculated and survey design variables added during data processing











Observation and Scope






Unit of observation


One adult BRFSS survey respondent




Population or objects represented


Adults age 18 or older living in noninstitutional settings within participating U.S. states and territories. The survey includes adults reached through landline or cellular telephone sampling who live in private residences or college housing. People living in institutions such as prisons, nursing homes, and long term care facilities are outside the target population




Time period covered


January through December 2024




Geographic area coverage


49 U.S. states, the District of Columbia, Guam, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Tennessee is not included in the 2024 public use file because it did not meet the minimum data requirements for inclusion











Variables and Data Structure






Main variables/fields


Demographic variables: age, sex, race/ethnicity, marital status, education, employment, and household income; health related variables: general health status, physical health days, mental health days, chronic conditions, health care access, exercise, smoking, alcohol use, and other health behaviors;




Data types included


Mostly coded categorical and numerical survey data. The dataset contains integer response codes, counts such as number of unhealthy days, demographic categories, yes/no indicators, geographic/reporting area identifiers, calculated variables, and survey design and weight variables




Direct measurements


Recorded survey responses, ex: reported age or age category, sex, race/ethnicity, marital status, education level, employment status, household income category, general health rating, number of days physical health was not good during the previous 30 days, and number of days mental health was not good during the previous 30 days




Possible proxy variables


Possible proxy variables include GENHLTH, PHYSHLTH, and MENTHLTH as indicators of health related quality of life, household income and education as indicators of socioeconomic position, employment status as indicator of economic circumstances, and some chronic condition/health access variables as possible indicators of broader health burden











Documentation






Documentation found


Official documentation is available from the CDC: https://www.cdc.gov/brfss/annual_data/annual_2024.html




Stated collection details


BRFSS is conducted continuously during the year using “random digit dialed landline and cellular telephone samples and computer assisted telephone interviewing”. Landline sampling selects an adult from an eligible household, while cellular sampling interviews eligible adults reached on cell phones. Proxy interviews are not used. States use a standardized core questionnaire and may add optional modules or state specific questions. After collection, responses are edited and coded, and survey weights are created to account for sampling probabilities, nonresponse, noncoverage, and demographic differences between the sample and the population. The 2024 public use file contains 457,670 records and 345 variables.

Source Identity

Smart Location Database




Domain/topic


transportation




Source type


Government database











Collection Context






Collector/producer


U.S. Environmental Protection Agency




Original purpose


To measure location efficacy and travel demand modeling




Collection method


Variables calculated from other data sources and summarized for each census block group




Record-creation event


EPA calculates and summarizes variables for each census block group











Observation and Scope






Unit of observation


One census block group




Population or objects represented


Census block groups avross U.S. along with demographics, jobs, and built enviornment of each




Time period covered


Not explicity stated but it was last updated in 2013 but uses 2019 Census Block Group




Geographic area coverage


Whole U.S. country











Variables and Data Structure






Main variables/fields


Demographic, employment, and built enviornment variables (residential and employment density, land use diversity, street design, access to destinations, and distance to transit)




Data types included


Numerical and geographic




Direct measurements


density and distance-to-transit variables are the closest to measuring something directly




Possible proxy variables


transit access, land use diversity, and walkability-type variables for quality of life











Documentation






Documentation found


Data.gov




Stated collection details


All the variables summarize demographic, employment, and built enviornment data for every block group. Update says uses 2019 Census Block Groups and new and expanded data sources. Calculation methods for some variables changed and specific sources and methods not stated
